panels.title: Facility health

targets.expr: max((ALERTS{alertstate="firing",component!="dev",severity="critical"} unless on(node) group by (node)(af_node_mount_result_fresh{node_pool="dev"})) * 3 or (ALERTS{alertstate="firing",component!="dev",severity="error"} unless on(node) group by (node)(af_node_mount_result_fresh{node_pool="dev"})) * 2 or (ALERTS{alertstate="firing",component!="dev",severity="warning"} unless on(node) group by (node)(af_node_mount_result_fresh{node_pool="dev"}))) or vector(0)

panels.description: Worst firing alert on cms-af-prod nodes. Dev nodes (a337) are monitored but excluded. Warnings: everything works, something is slow or filling up. Degraded: a user-facing function is broken. Outage: users cannot get in.

panels.description: Green: OK. Orange: partial, some prod nodes affected. Red: down. Evaluated on cms-af-prod nodes only; each row shows history over the selected time range. AF nodes and the four mounts are fractions of prod nodes passing. Ceph is the worst of its monitor, manager, metadata-server, CSI-driver and OSD groups on Geddes, as Kubernetes reports them; OSDs only count once availability drops below 90%.

panels.description: Only the cms-af-prod and cms-af-dev pools are listed; prod nodes count toward facility health, dev nodes do not. Reserved: sum of CPU/RAM requests of all pods on the node, what the scheduler counts. Free: what a new session or Dask worker can still request. Busy: actual use right now; blank on nodes without node-exporter. The footer sums the count columns over all listed nodes.

panels.title: CPU: reserved vs. used
panels.description: Cores on AF nodes. Solid: reserved by requests. Dashed: actually used. Other: everything in the cms namespace that is not a session or a Dask worker (hub, gateways, inference servers, monitoring).

panels.title: RAM: reserved vs. used
panels.description: Solid: reserved by requests. Dashed: working-set memory actually used.

panels.title: GPUs: reserved vs. used
panels.description: Devices: whole T4 cards and A100 MIG slices count as one each. Used is the sum of graphics-engine activity, i.e. device-equivalents busy. Other: inference servers and anything else holding a GPU.

panels.description: All Dask Gateway clusters on Kubernetes. Idle workers hold reserved cores while doing nothing.

panels.title: Cluster activity by user
panels.description: Per user: orange while any of their clusters is running tasks, grey while a cluster exists but runs nothing, blank when they have no cluster. Long grey stretches are reserved cores doing nothing.

panels.title: Utilization right now
panels.description: Workers busy: share of workers that are not idle. Cores computing: task compute time per second divided by the cores reserved by all workers. Both low with many workers means capacity is reserved but wasted.

panels.title: Clusters

targets.expr: label_replace(((sum by (pod)(dask_scheduler_workers) > 0) and on(pod) (sum by (pod)(dask_scheduler_clients) == 0) and on(pod) (sum by (pod)(dask_scheduler_tasks{state="processing"}) == 0)) > bool 0, "cluster", "$1", "pod", "dask-scheduler-([0-9a-f]{32})")

panels.description: One row per Dask Gateway cluster on Kubernetes. IDLE: workers allocated, no client connected, nothing running; those cores block everyone else until the cluster is shut down or adaptive scaling releases them.

panels.title: Cores reserved per user, right now

targets.expr: sum by (user)( sum by (cluster)(label_replace(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace="cms",pod=~"dask-worker-.*",resource="cpu"}, "cluster", "$1", "pod", "dask-worker-([0-9a-f]{32})-.*")) * on(cluster) group_left(user) (sum by (user, cluster)(label_replace(dask_scheduler_workers, "cluster", "$1", "pod", "dask-scheduler-([0-9a-f]{32})")) > bool -1) )

panels.description: Cores requested by each user's Dask workers on Kubernetes. Compare with the activity timeline above: a large bar for a grey row is capacity nobody can use.

panels.title: Workers by state, right now
panels.description: As reported by the schedulers. Idle: nothing to do. Partially saturated and saturated: working. Paused: over the memory limit, not accepting tasks. Retiring: being scaled down.

panels.title: Core-hours computed per user, time range
panels.description: Task compute time delivered to each user over the selected time range, in core-hours. This is the useful work done, as opposed to cores merely reserved.

panels.title: Cores busy: computing vs. transferring data
panels.description: Task-seconds per second summed over all workers; above the worker count means multi-threaded workers. Transferring high relative to computing means the work is network-bound.

panels.title: Workers by saturation
panels.description: As reported by the schedulers. Idle workers are reserved cores doing nothing; saturated workers have more tasks than threads.
Maximum near 100% means workers are about to be killed for memory. Legend hidden: series are cluster ids, see the table above; hover for values.

max by (cluster_name) (
  sum by (pod, cluster_name) (
    label_replace(
      container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"dask-worker-.*", container="dask-worker"},

      "pod",

    )

)

avg by (cluster_name) (
  sum by (pod, cluster_name) (
    label_replace(
      container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"dask-worker-.*", container="dask-worker"},
      "cluster_name",
      "$1",
      "pod",
      "dask-worker-([0-9a-f]{32})-.*"
    )

  /
  sum by (pod, cluster_name) (
